align_above_source.goal: Align over the exposed upper bottle neck below the cork. Use a downward finger approach and keep the wrist housing above the bottle top. Do not use a deep body grasp.
align_above_source.exit: Advance when the currently selected source-minus-hand X and Y are both within -10 to +10 mm inclusive. This is coarse horizontal alignment only. Fine grasp orientation and grasp height are judged in the next nearer-approach stage, not certified here.

control_contract.translation: Coarse horizontal alignment to the actor-selected visual reference.
control_contract.height: Keep suitable overhead clearance; being above the source is not a reason to rise further.
control_contract.exit: Advance when the currently selected source-minus-hand X and Y are both within -10 to +10 mm inclusive. This is coarse horizontal alignment only. Fine grasp orientation and grasp height are judged in the next nearer-approach stage, not certified here.
control_contract.orientation: Judge rotation separately from XYZ position and distance. A far-away hand can already have suitable orientation. The earlier orientation assessment is an unverified hypothesis, not a veto of completed coarse X/Y alignment.

close.goal: Attempt closure around the positioned grasp region; secure holding will be tested next.
close.exit: A close command has actually been executed. Advance provisionally unless fresh RGB clearly shows a missed grasp; contact proof is not required before the attempt.

control_contract.translation: Keep the positioned hand still during closure.
control_contract.exit: Closure has actually been attempted; lift or turn tests engagement.

descend_to_source.goal: Bring the open finger faces alongside the exposed upper bottle neck, below the cork, while keeping the wrist housing clear. Select that neck region from current RGB rather than the wider body.
descend_to_source.exit: The selected bottle grasp-region reference is within +/-3mm on X/Y and -8 to 8mm on Z, matching the axis questions, with no clear current-RGB contradiction to a closure attempt. This is not proven contact or holding.

lift.goal: Test that the bottle follows the closing hand, and establish enough clearance to start transporting it to the rack. Further vertical rise is not needed once this is visibly achieved.
lift.exit: Current and previous RGB show the bottle following the hand off the table, with useful transport clearance. A matched visible-feature motion may support this judgment, but hand motion alone is insufficient.

align_source_above_receiver.goal: Carry the actual bottle toward the slatted WOODEN cradle. Place the bottle lengthwise along the inclined rack channel rather than keeping it upright over a table. Choose a visible bottle BODY reference for placement, not merely the held neck. Judge the bottle long axis against the rack channel in current RGB and the actual placement demonstration.
align_source_above_receiver.exit: The bottle body is above the wooden cradle with transport clearance and its lengthwise orientation fits the inclined support. A hand-to-rack or neck-only coincidence is not sufficient.

control_contract.references: B dots are current brown-component surface samples inside the rack identity region, excluding the measured own robot. Colour alone does not establish identity. Select a dot actually on the broad slatted wooden cradle, not a narrow upright, wall, table or unrelated furniture. Choose a visible bottle BODY feature for placement and compare the body with the cradle; neither a dot nor a hand overlap is a complete target pose.
control_contract.orientation: The upright bottle posture used for lifting is not automatically the rack placement posture. Judge actual bottle long-axis alignment to the inclined cradle. No desired rotation, target angle or angle error is supplied.

align_above_source.z: Is a world-Z clearance correction needed during horizontal alignment? Current source surface minus hand Z is {z_mm} mm. When the hand is already well above the source with visible clearance, hold Z; do not rise merely because this is an above-source stage. Positive is up, negative is down.
align_above_source.transition: Current coarse source-minus-hand X={x_mm} mm, Y={y_mm} mm. Is coarse horizontal alignment complete? Advance when BOTH numbers lie within -10 to +10 mm inclusive. Do not require contact, grasp-height alignment, or perfect orientation here. Those belong to the next nearer-approach stage. A previous approach_mismatch label alone is not a reason to keep holding when X/Y are aligned. Continue if either current reference difference remains outside the band or is unknown.
align_above_source.rx: Measured own_tool_geometry.grip_site_local_Z_world_unit is the direction the fingers point, not a desired object angle. Both grasp examples use top-down fingers. If its Z component is below -0.95 and current RGB does not reveal an actual tilt mismatch, HOLD this tilt channel. Pure XYZ offset never requires a tilt. If the approach is sideways, use the demonstrated motion effect and current own vector to restore a downward approach. Current goal: {stage_goal} Roll about fixed world X: with fingers nearly down, positive tilts them toward +Y and negative toward -Y. From current RGB and measured own-hand axes, choose positive, negative, or hold to fit the physical grasp/support geometry. Ignore pure XYZ position error when judging rotation. Hold when the posture is suitable.
align_above_source.ry: Measured own_tool_geometry.grip_site_local_Z_world_unit is the direction the fingers point, not a desired object angle. Both grasp examples use top-down fingers. If its Z component is below -0.95 and current RGB does not reveal an actual tilt mismatch, HOLD this tilt channel. Pure XYZ offset never requires a tilt. If the approach is sideways, use the demonstrated motion effect and current own vector to restore a downward approach. Current goal: {stage_goal} Pitch about fixed world Y: with fingers nearly down, positive tilts them toward -X and negative toward +X. From current RGB and measured own-hand axes, choose positive, negative, or hold to fit the physical grasp/support geometry. Ignore pure XYZ position error when judging rotation. Hold when the posture is suitable.
align_above_source.rz: Current goal: {stage_goal} Yaw about fixed world Z changes horizontal jaw heading; it cannot turn a downward finger approach into a sideways approach. Positive is counterclockwise viewed from above. From current RGB and measured own-hand axes, choose positive, negative, or hold to fit the physical grasp/support geometry. Ignore pure XYZ position error when judging rotation. Hold when the posture is suitable.

descend_to_source.z: Current selected bottle grasp-region feature minus hand height Z={z_mm}mm. The positioning band is -8 to 8mm. Choose negative Z (DOWN) below -8mm; choose positive Z (UP) above 8mm; hold inside the band. This same height relationship is used by the stage exit. Current RGB must confirm the selected physical region and downward fingers; a surface coordinate does not prove contact.
descend_to_source.transition: Current source-reference minus hand X={x_mm}mm, Y={y_mm}mm, Z={z_mm}mm. Continue if X or Y is outside +/-3mm, or Z outside -8 to 8mm. When these SAME axis-positioning bands are reached, advance to ATTEMPT closure unless current RGB clearly contradicts the intended bottle grasp. Do not require already-proven contact. Unknown values are not zero.
descend_to_source.rx: Measured own_tool_geometry.grip_site_local_Z_world_unit is the direction the fingers point, not a desired object angle. Both grasp examples use top-down fingers. If its Z component is below -0.95 and current RGB does not reveal an actual tilt mismatch, HOLD this tilt channel. Pure XYZ offset never requires a tilt. If the approach is sideways, use the demonstrated motion effect and current own vector to restore a downward approach. Current goal: {stage_goal} Roll about fixed world X: with fingers nearly down, positive tilts them toward +Y and negative toward -Y. From current RGB and measured own-hand axes, choose positive, negative, or hold to fit the physical grasp/support geometry. Ignore pure XYZ position error when judging rotation. Hold when the posture is suitable.

If its Z component is below -0.95 and current RGB does not reveal an actual tilt mismatch, HOLD this tilt channel. Pure XYZ offset never requires a tilt. If the approach is sideways, use the demonstrated motion effect and current own vector to restore a downward approach. Current goal: {stage_goal} Pitch about fixed world Y: with fingers nearly down, positive tilts them toward -X and negative toward +X. From current RGB and measured own-hand axes, choose positive, negative, or hold to fit the physical grasp/support geometry. Ignore pure XYZ position error when judging rotation. Hold when the posture is suitable.
descend_to_source.rz: Current goal: {stage_goal} Yaw about fixed world Z changes horizontal jaw heading; it cannot turn a downward finger approach into a sideways approach. Positive is counterclockwise viewed from above. From current RGB and measured own-hand axes, choose positive, negative, or hold to fit the physical grasp/support geometry. Ignore pure XYZ position error when judging rotation. Hold when the posture is suitable.
descend_to_source.x: Current RGB-selected source-reference minus hand X is {x_mm}mm. Choose positive when this number is above +3mm, negative below -3mm, and hold within -3 to +3mm. This is the same coarse reference band as the near-stage exit. Verify the reference is on the intended fin or upper neck from current RGB; a wrong body/base reference is not a valid alignment goal.
descend_to_source.y: Current RGB-selected source-reference minus hand Y is {y_mm}mm. Choose positive when this number is above +3mm, negative below -3mm, and hold within -3 to +3mm. This is the same coarse reference band as the near-stage exit. Verify the reference is on the intended fin or upper neck from current RGB; a wrong body/base reference is not a valid alignment goal.

close.gripper: The goal is to ATTEMPT closure around the positioned region. Last executed gripper command={gripper_command}; current pad-centre separation={pad_separation_mm} mm. Choose close if closure has not been attempted; retain close if already closing/closed. Open only if visible recovery requires release. Closure is not proof of holding.
close.transition: Last executed gripper command={gripper_command}. If it is open, continue this stage so closure can actually execute. After a close command has executed, advance provisionally to lift/turn unless fresh RGB clearly shows a missed grasp. Do not demand already-proven attachment before the test.

lift.gripper: Retain the close command while testing whether the bottle follows the hand. Open only for an intentional visible recovery.
lift.transition: This stage has executed {stage_steps} physical steps. If zero, continue to execute the active upward test after closure. Otherwise compare actual source RGB/matched-feature motion with measured own motion. If the bottle follows off the table with useful transport clearance, ADVANCE now; if it clearly stays behind or drops, restart. No contact proof is required before the test and own motion alone is not attachment.
lift.z: The purpose of this stage is an ACTIVE lift test after closure. Look at last_actions: if closure has executed but no upward test has yet executed in Lift, choose POSITIVE Z to test whether the bottle follows; do not require an already-proven grasp before this test. After an upward test, keep positive only while actual source table clearance is insufficient. Hold once the bottle itself follows off the table with transport clearance, and let transition advance. If the source stays behind, transition should restart rather than hold indefinitely.

align_source_above_receiver.z: Is a world-Z clearance correction needed for the HELD BOTTLE above the rack? Current selected rack support minus selected bottle surface Z={receiver_z_mm} mm. Use actual bottle thickness and current RGB, not gripper height alone. Positive moves the held object up, negative down; hold when transport clearance is suitable.
align_source_above_receiver.transition: Does the actual bottle BODY have clearance above the wooden cradle and a suitable lengthwise orientation along its inclined channel? Receiver-minus-selected-body X={receiver_x_mm}mm, Y={receiver_y_mm}mm are supporting reference measurements, not proof that the whole bottle fits. Advance to lowering only when the visible body fits the support direction and horizontal location; continue for actual translation or rotation correction. Do not treat an upright bottle above the rack as already aligned.
align_source_above_receiver.rx: For an attached upright bottle whose upward body axis is +Z, positive world-X roll tilts that upward axis toward -Y; negative roll tilts it toward +Y. A downward finger vector changes oppositely because it starts at -Z. This is a generic rotation example, not the desired bottle orientation. Use the CURRENT bottle axis versus the inclined wooden cradle, own-hand axes and actual motion examples to choose positive, negative or hold for roll. Ignore XYZ distance.
align_source_above_receiver.ry: For an attached upright bottle whose upward body axis is +Z, positive world-Y pitch tilts that upward axis toward +X; negative pitch tilts it toward -X. A downward finger vector changes oppositely because it starts at -Z. This is a generic rotation example, not a target angle. Use CURRENT bottle-long-axis versus wooden-cradle geometry and actual examples to choose positive, negative or hold for pitch. Ignore XYZ distance.
align_source_above_receiver.rz: Positive world-Z yaw rotates a horizontal +X direction toward +Y, and +Y toward -X. It does not tilt a perfectly vertical bottle. Use current bottle orientation versus the inclined wooden channel to choose positive, negative or hold for yaw; do not copy the rotation sign of a different starting posture.

lower_to_place.z: Which world-Z motion brings the HELD BOTTLE into a suitable supported relationship with the rack? Selected rack support minus bottle surface Z={receiver_z_mm} mm. Positive is up, negative down. Account for visible body thickness: these are observed skin features, not centres or a contact certificate. Hold when a release attempt is visually reasonable.
lower_to_place.transition: Advance to release when the bottle appears seated in the rack support channel or available views support a reasonable release attempt. Continue if an obvious unsupported gap remains. Do not demand a hidden contact flag.

release.gripper: Open the fingers to release the manipulated object or control. Last executed gripper command={gripper_command}. Retain open once opening has actually executed.
release.transition: If last executed gripper command={gripper_command} is still close, continue so opening can execute. After opening is observed or measured, advance to inspection. Opening alone is not task completion.
